description:
Programme or Project Overview

Utrecht University invites applications for a postdoc on multi-risk adaptation pathways for river delta systems. The project studies how delta regions can plan for interacting hazards, such as floods, droughts and salinisation, rather than treating risks one at a time, and develops pathway approaches that keep adaptation options open under deep uncertainty.

The postdoc will combine risk modelling, scenario analysis and adaptation-pathway methods, working with delta case studies and stakeholders. The research connects hydrology, systems analysis and governance studies, and contributes to international debates on delta management and climate adaptation. The appointment is a salaried postdoctoral contract under the CAO-NU collective agreement.

Candidate profile

Applicants hold a PhD in hydrology, environmental systems analysis, water governance or a related field, with demonstrable skills in quantitative modelling and scenario methods. Experience with stakeholder-engaged research and dynamic adaptive policy pathways is an advantage. The working language is English, and the postdoc joins an active water and climate research community.

Highlights

  • Multi-risk analysis in river deltas
  • Adaptation pathways under deep uncertainty
  • Flood, drought and salinisation interactions
  • Scenario and systems modelling
  • Stakeholder-engaged delta research
  • Salaried postdoc under the CAO-NU agreement
